question:
**Case Study: Production Consistency with Dependent Resources**

A factory manufactures three products P, Q, R using three machines. The machine hour requirement matrix is:

$M = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 3 & 3 \\ 6 & 6 & 6 \\ 9 & 9 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

Let $x, y, z$ represent units of P, Q, R respectively. If the factory has 36, 72, and 108 machine hours for machines 1, 2, and 3 respectively:

**(a)** Express the system as $MX = B$.

**(b)** Show, using determinant and matrix theory, whether a unique solution for (P, Q, R) exists.

**(c)** Suggest a practical limitation observed in this setup and what it implies for resource management.
explanation:
**(a) System:**
$M \cdot X = B$
$\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 3 & 3 \\ 6 & 6 & 6 \\ 9 & 9 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 36 \\ 72 \\ 108 \end{bmatrix}$

**(b) Determinant and Existence:**
All rows of $M$ are multiples of the first.
Determinant of such a matrix is zero since the rows are linearly dependent.
Thus, $|M|=0$ which implies the system does not have a unique solution.
The system is either inconsistent or has infinitely many solutions if $(adj\ M)B=0$.

**(c) Practical Limitation:**
The material requirements are perfectly proportional.
Thus, increasing production of one product linearly increases all others.
In practice, the system is underdetermined.
Any choice of $(x,y,z)$ with $x+y+z=12$ will work, but the exact allocation among products cannot be uniquely decided by machine hours alone.
This reflects insufficiently independent resource constraints — a limitation in the design of factory allocation or data collection.
Unique resource management would require linearly independent constraints.

options.A:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}3&3&3\\6&6&6\\9&9&9\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}36\\72\\108\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|\ne0$, the system has a unique solution.
(c) Machine hours are independent, so resource allocation is uniquely determined.
options.B:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}3&3&3\\6&6&6\\9&9&9\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, and $B=\begin{bmatrix}36\\72\\108\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $R_2=2R_1$ and $R_3=3R_1$, $|M|=0$, so no unique solution exists; the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions satisfying $x+y+z=12$.
(c) The constraints are dependent, so machine hours alone cannot decide a unique production plan.
options.C:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}36&72&108\\3&3&3\\6&6&6\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|=0$, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.
(c) No production plan can satisfy the available hours.
options.D:
(a) $MX=B$, where $B=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since the determinant is zero, the only possible solution is $x=y=z=0$.
(c) The factory must stop production.
